slides.title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
slides.highlight: This work introduces CE-CM and CE-CM-Div to infer hidden partner capabilities and adapt to human unpredictability, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and infer partner intent for ad-hoc teaming.

card.one_liner: A Bayesian method for agents to infer task-invariant partner capabilities to adapt coordination across multiple tasks.
card.key_idea: CE-CM uses simulation-based approximate Bayesian computation to infer latent capability vectors from observed trajectories, inducing capability-conditioned models for joint planning with decentralized execution.
card.evaluation: Tested in TidyUP (PDDL) and Overcooked simulators, plus an offline study of 225 human trajectories. Results show rapid capability recovery and improved coordination.
card.limitation: Standard CE-CM is brittle to suboptimal or diverse human behavior, requiring the CE-CM-Div extension to avoid rejecting valid capability hypotheses.

slides.title: Humanoid Companion Robot Market Projected to Reach US$1.1bn by 2030
slides.highlight: The rising demand for caregiving and emotional support is driving growth in the humanoid companion robot market. This trend aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making
slides.tldr: SOCIAL SIMULATION OF HIGH-STAKES MILITARY DECISIONS
slides.highlight: WOPR provides a verifiable rules engine and private-channel negotiation for social simulations, supporting the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: WOPR is a social-simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making using a verifiable rules engine.
card.key_idea: A deterministic, replay-validated engine instantiated with the game 'Nuclear War', featuring a decision-point contract, a four-rung communication ladder, and four command-and-control faction archetypes.
card.evaluation: Verified via a 240-game sweep confirming seeded outcomes are preserved across engine changes; results are deterministic and replay-checkable.
card.limitation: Early-stage work; no controlled studies on agent behavior, no large-scale press evaluation, and commitments are not automatically enforced.

slides.title: Cocktail-Talker: Multi-Speaker Dialog Modeling in Noisy Social Environments with Turn Action GRPO
slides.tldr: MULTI-SPEAKER DIALOG MODELING IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a speech LLM framework that uses action tokens to decide whether to respond, listen, or ignore in multi-speaker social settings. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and engagement in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Cocktail-Talker enables speech assistants to selectively respond, listen, or ignore in noisy multi-speaker environments.
card.key_idea: A Qwen2.5-Omni-based framework using three action tokens, trained via supervised finetuning and GRPO reinforcement learning on simulated multi-speaker dialogs from the Cocktail-DialogGen pipeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on seen and unseen environments using binary Respond/Silent accuracy and response quality metrics (METEOR, ROUGE-L). Results show significant improvement over baselines.
card.limitation: The system is not streaming, assumes fixed turn boundaries, and lacks visual or spatial cues for speaker inference.

slides.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
slides.tldr: HYBRID ATTENTION ESTIMATION FOR ADAPTIVE HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline combining geometric and semantic perception to regulate adaptive interaction behaviors in an expressive robotic head, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A hybrid attention-estimation pipeline for an expressive robotic head to enable adaptive human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast geometric layer (MediaPipe head-pose) for real-time state regulation with a VLM-based semantic layer (LLaVA-Phi3) for contextual interpretation via a finite state machine.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants across 40 trials. Results showed reliable interaction starts and successful adaptive pause/resume behaviors in distraction scenarios.
card.limitation: Controlled experimental setup, small participant sample, and lack of manual frame-level ground truth for attention labels.

slides.title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a simulation-trained controller that addresses human-device co-adaptation to reduce metabolic cost during walking, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on coadaptive loops and human proficiency.

card.one_liner: SMAT reduces walking metabolic cost by 19.7% relative to a passive hip exoskeleton without subject-specific retraining.
card.key_idea: A four-stage curriculum (gait learning, mass adaptation, timing pre-training, and co-adaptation) trains a musculoskeletal human actor and exoskeleton actor concurrently in physics-based simulation.
card.evaluation: Validated with 8 healthy adults using indirect calorimetry and biomechanical analysis; results showed significant metabolic reduction (p < 0.001) and high positive-power ratio (0.98).

slides.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics
slides.highlight: TIDES provides a longitudinal dataset of real-world team interactions with annotations on emergent roles and interaction types, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and group dynamics.

card.one_liner: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of university project teams used to model multi-party social dynamics.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 75,971 utterances with socio-structural annotations (interaction types, emergent roles, and development stages) to improve next-speaker prediction and study team evolution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via next-speaker/intention prediction and human preference. Fine-tuning improved speaker prediction (64.53%) and performed competitively on the AMI Meeting Corpus.
card.limitation: Improved structural prediction (next-speaker) does not necessarily translate to more natural or coherent utterance generation according to human evaluators.

slides.title: Google Unveils Gemini Robotics 2: Humanoid Robots Collaborate to Tidy Rooms
slides.highlight: Google has introduced Gemini Robotics 2, featuring humanoid robots that collaborate to tidy rooms, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: VISA: A Structured Description Protocol for Agent-Based Simulation Models Towards Machine Reproducibility
slides.tldr: STRUCTURED PROTOCOL FOR MACHINE-REPRODUCIBLE AGENT-BASED MODELS
slides.highlight: VISA introduces a symbol-based description protocol and LLM-executable skills to make agent-based models machine-parseable and reproducible. This supports MIMIC by providing a framework for the formal specification and validation of agent models used in societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: VISA is a symbol-based, table-driven protocol designed to make agent-based models machine-reproducible and unambiguous.
card.key_idea: It specifies models via eight interconnected tables (four agent-level, four model-level) using mathematical notation and nineteen consistency rules to enable automated parsing and code generation.
card.evaluation: Validated on three external ABMs; successfully reproduced two cross-language (NetLogo to Python) and captured one industrial AnyLogic model, identifying specific proprietary reproduction blockers.
card.limitation: Reproduction can still be blocked by proprietary libraries or unavailable data, which the protocol identifies but cannot bypass.

slides.title: Learning Social Robot Navigation By Sensing Human Legs
slides.tldr: SOCIAL ROBOT NAVIGATION VIA LEG SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces CALF, a neural architecture that interprets leg motion from LiDAR scans to improve social compliance in robot navigation, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: CALF is an end-to-end RL policy for social robot navigation sensing human legs via 2D LiDAR.
card.key_idea: A hybrid architecture combining 1D-CNNs for feature extraction, temporal self-attention for leg motion inference, and an MLP, trained in a custom JAX-based simulator with realistic gait dynamics.
card.evaluation: Compared against classical and RL baselines in LegNav simulator and validated via zero-shot deployment on a TurtleBot 4 for social compliance and safety.

slides.title: TacPrint: A Wearable Fingertip Tactile Sensor for Human-to-Robot Contact Reproduction
slides.tldr: WEARABLE FINGERTIP TACTILE SENSOR FOR CONTACT REPRODUCTION
slides.highlight: TacPrint enables fine-grained capture of fingertip interactions for human-to-robot skill transfer, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills through force-based sensing.

card.one_liner: TacPrint is a low-cost wearable fingertip sensor for high-fidelity human-to-robot contact reproduction in manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A 24-channel capacitive sensor with taxel-aligned silicone protrusions uses an LSTM-based real-to-sim-to-real pipeline to estimate dense 35x26 contact-depth maps from sparse signals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled indentations, human-to-robot replay (grasping/wiping), and closed-loop grasping. Results show high success rates (up to 91.67%) and low depth error (0.085mm).
card.limitation: Sparse 24-channel input limits detailed shape reconstruction; predictions may retain training indenter characteristics and lack full pixel-level deformation validation.

slides.title: Recompute or Reuse? Diagnosing and Mitigating Textual Shortcuts in VLM Self-Reflection
slides.tldr: MITIGATING TEXTUAL SHORTCUTS IN VLM SELF-REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This research identifies how prior chains of thought create textual shortcuts that hinder visual recomputation, offering a method to isolate fresh computation for better self-reflection. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: VLMs often reuse stale reasoning from prior chains-of-thought as shortcuts instead of recomputing from current images.
card.key_idea: Identifies evidence-bearing prior reasoning as a 'textual shortcut' and introduces Fresh-State Attention Firewall (FSAF), a training-free attention mask isolating fresh computation from prior CoT.
card.evaluation: Tested 16 VLMs using VS-Bench counterfactual pairs; FSAF (on 5 Qwen models) raised visual update rate from 35.28% to 53.61%.
card.limitation: FSAF suppresses stale-answer control but does not guarantee current-answer recovery for every sample pair.

slides.title: Beyond Feeling Better: Capability-Sustaining Emotional Dialogue as a Longitudinal Research Paradigm
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a longitudinal paradigm for emotional dialogue that focuses on sustaining user capacities for social connection and emotion regulation, contributing to HyECHO's goals in modeling engagement and group norms.

card.one_liner: Proposes CSED, a longitudinal paradigm to sustain user psychological capabilities rather than just providing immediate relief.
card.key_idea: CSED shifts the unit of inquiry to the full interaction lifecycle, using six design commitments and four evaluation timescales to preserve autonomy, resilience, and social connectedness.
card.evaluation: Audit of 91 papers and 300 ESConv turns; found 95% of system papers are relief-oriented and none evaluate longitudinal capability outcomes.
card.limitation: Relies on latent state proxies; longitudinal measurement introduces privacy/surveillance risks and potential conflicts between immediate relief and long-term capability.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC GOVERNANCE FOR VERIFIABLE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for verifiable AI agents in digital twin ecosystems, aligning with MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic agent models and societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A decentralized governance framework ensuring verifiable identity and policy compliance for AI agents in digital twin ecosystems.
card.key_idea: Binds LLM agents to symbolic profiles using ontology-grounded capabilities and W3C Verifiable Credentials, validated via blockchain smart contracts for auditable, policy-aware participation.
card.evaluation: Tested with 42 cases (security, scalability, overhead) using a healthcare prototype; achieved 100% attack detection and O(1) verification complexity.
card.limitation: Focuses on admission governance and provenance; does not verify the actual quality or correctness of the agent's clinical recommendations.

slides.title: StreamTalk: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Key-Pose Anchoring
slides.highlight: StreamTalk introduces a closed-loop framework for real-time 3D gesture generation that reduces drift using key-pose anchoring, supporting the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: StreamTalk prevents long-term motion drift in streaming co-speech gestures using a closed-loop key-pose anchoring framework.
card.key_idea: A generate-retrieve-refine cycle uses a speaker-specific database to retrieve tail key-poses as destination anchors, supported by Stochastic Anchor Masking and a part-aware DiT architecture.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT2 benchmark using FGD, BC, and Diversity; results show state-of-the-art motion quality and real-time performance at 76 FPS.

slides.title: When Robots Exchange Meaning: A Demo of Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications for Collaborative Robotics
slides.highlight: This work presents a semantic communication testbed for collaborative robotics that reduces data payload via VQ-VAE tokens to support semantic mapping and object-level interaction, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied AI.

card.one_liner: A robot-edge testbed demonstrating goal-oriented semantic communication for collaborative robotics using VQ-VAE visual compression.
card.key_idea: Robot-side VQ-VAE encodes RGB frames into tokens, which an edge node reconstructs to perform RTAB-Map SLAM and YOLO-based semantic object mapping for mission control.
card.evaluation: Offline tests showed 21.7–21.9 dB PSNR and a 42.67x reduction in model-input RGB bytes. Results are presented as a proof-of-concept demo.
card.limitation: Lacks detailed runtime comparisons, wireless latency characterization over 5G/Open RAN, energy consumption analysis, and multi-robot task execution evaluation.

slides.title: FasTac: A Curved Multispectral Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for High-Speed High-Precision 3D Shape and Force Perception
slides.highlight: FasTac enables high-precision 3D shape and three-axis force perception, supporting the physics-based force estimation and tactile sensing required for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: FasTac is a curved multispectral tactile sensor for high-speed 3D shape and three-axis force perception.
card.key_idea: Combines RGB-NIR photometric stereo for 3D reconstruction, HyperForce dynamic convolution for position-aware force estimation, and FPGA hardware acceleration for low-latency processing.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via depth MAE (0.0415 mm), force NMAE (2.39%–2.74%), and latency (1.09 ms on FPGA). Validated through multi-object reconstruction and feedback grasping.

slides.title: Cross-Task Dissociation in Frontier Vision-Language Model Theory of Mind
slides.tldr: VLMS SHOW INCONSISTENT THEORY-OF-MIND PROFILES ACROSS TASKS
slides.highlight: This research evaluates how frontier VLMs perform on perspective-taking and intention attribution tasks, showing a lack of a coherent Theory-of-Mind profile. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of developing agents that can infer partners' intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: Frontier VLMs show fragmented Theory-of-Mind profiles, failing to align with a single human reference group across tasks.
card.key_idea: Evaluated nine VLMs using a paired-task design: the Keysar Director Task (visual perspective-taking) and Frith-Happé animated triangles (intention attribution) to detect cross-task dissociation.
card.evaluation: Nine frontier VLMs were tested on psychology-derived benchmarks. Results showed most models align with different human reference groups (TD-adult vs. HF-ASD-adult) across the two tasks.
card.limitation: Animated-triangles scoring relies on LLM-as-rater rather than humans, creating a measurement noise floor; only two psychology tasks were used.

slides.title: Solitics Launches Saai for Retail Banking Customer Engagement
slides.highlight: The launch of Saai for automating customer engagement provides insights into agentic AI's role in managing interactions, relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

slides.title: Using Theory of Mind to Arbitrate between Social and Non-social Learning
slides.tldr: THEORY OF MIND FOR SOCIAL LEARNING ARBITRATION
slides.highlight: This research proposes a Rational Mentalizing model that uses Theory of Mind to determine when to engage in social learning versus direct experience, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent.

card.one_liner: A Rational Mentalizing model uses Theory of Mind to optimize the trade-off between social and non-social learning.
card.key_idea: The model employs Bayesian Theory of Mind to infer others' goals and beliefs, weighing the expected utility of observing agents against the cost of independent exploration.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via four human experiments in a grid-game; the model achieved high concordance (CCC=0.89) compared to three ablations lacking utility or mentalizing components.
card.limitation: The model systematically underpredicts the absolute amount of observation and movement humans perform, potentially omitting curiosity-driven or hedging behaviors.

slides.title: Could Agentic AI Bring American Manufacturing Back?
slides.highlight: Explores the potential of agentic AI to revitalize American manufacturing, relating to MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation and skill acquisition in industrial settings.

slides.title: CHILL-Harness: Counterfactual Harness Learning for Efficient Reasoning in Long-Horizon Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces CHILL-Harness, which uses causal learning to adaptively orchestrate agent workflows, improving execution efficiency for long-horizon tasks. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models and societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: CHILL-Harness uses causal learning to adaptively orchestrate agent workflows, reducing token and time costs.
card.key_idea: It employs Causal Intervention Effect Learning (CIEL) to estimate workflow advantages and Advantage-Realizing Causal Orchestration (ARCO) to execute only success-preserving, high-advantage adaptations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on GAIA, SWE-bench Verified, and Terminal-Bench 2.0 against baselines like Terminus-KIRA; results show preserved/improved success with significantly lower token consumption.
